name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,547

clue.text: Strong booze in pack partly emptied

indicators.note: emptying a word takes out its insides, leaving just the two letters at its ends

blocks.note: in rugby the forwards bound together are the pack, or scrum
the word with its middle removed keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Somebody finds a potent drink stashed in a backpack that has been half unpacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrum is the huddle of forwards in rugby, also called the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumpy is rough, often very potent farmhouse cider from the West of England.

clue.text: One certainly having legs to stretch forward on the ball

blocks.note: to crane is to stretch the neck forward to see
fly is informal British for alert or sharp

explanation.surface: A footballer with long legs reaches out to take the ball forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like football; the insect is known in Britain as the daddy-long-legs for its very long, spindly legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly is a gangly insect whose long thin legs are its most noticeable feature.

clue.text: Submarine needs anti-rust treatment endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the phrase's word is cut off

blocks.note: underseal is the protective coating sprayed under a car body against rust

explanation.surface: A submarine needs protecting against corrosion, though the job never quite gets finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Underseal is the British name for the coating Americans call undercoating, applied to a car's underside.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective describes anything existing or happening beneath the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Scotch, superior flavour mostly, drink not from bottles

indicators.note: most of a word but not all of it, so its last letter is dropped
to bottle something is to shut it inside, so one piece holds the others

blocks.note: pop is a fizzy soft drink
U means upper class, or superior
a synonym
the opposite of from is to

explanation.surface: A connoisseur insists the finest whisky flavour is never served out of bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like the whisky but is the verb meaning to end or thwart. U is the old British label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to halt it decisively, the same meaning as this phrase.

clue.text: Owed pounds in honourable affair

blocks.note: money owed is due
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: An unpaid debt of a few pounds turns into a question of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel was fought to settle a matter of honour, so it is an affair of honour between gentlemen.

clue.text: Fish pub served during harvest

indicators.note: something served during an event is set down in the middle of it

blocks.note: to mow is to cut down a crop
a synonym

explanation.surface: Fish was on the pub menu while the farmers were bringing in the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: A minnow is a tiny freshwater fish of the carp family, common in streams.

clue.text: Riddles from two sons outside school

indicators.note: the letters stand outside, one on each side, wrapping the other word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son, twice
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A pair of boys bring home puzzles they picked up outside the school gates.
explanation.walkthrough: Riddles here is the verb: a riddle is a coarse sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle soil or gravel is to pass it through a sieve, which strains it.

clue.text: Publish charter again?

blocks.note: the prefix meaning again
to charter a boat or plane is to hire or lease it

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second reading splits the word as re-lease, to charter once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a record, film or statement is to make it public, issuing it to everyone.

clue.text: Cast informed

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: given a role in a film
second meaning: brought up to date with the facts

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a pair, perhaps a cast that was briefed; each separately gives the phrase, one literally and one idiomatically.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fully briefed, and literally an actor cast in a film has been given a place in the movie.

clue.text: Order what you need to make friend?

definitions.text: what you need to make friend?

blocks.note: first meaning: an official command or instruction

blocks.clueFragment: what you need to make friend?
blocks.note: second meaning, read playfully: a social outing between two men, which is how many male friendships begin

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the word as man date, a slangy term for a platonic outing between men; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an authoritative command, such as one a government receives from voters or issues to officials.

clue.text: Fruit without starter scoffed after good stretch

indicators.note: with no starter means the opening letter of the word is taken away
one piece is placed following the other in the answer

blocks.note: a melon is a fruit
G is the abbreviation for good
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: Someone skips the starter, wolfs down some fruit and then has a good long stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to lengthen, making something longer by drawing it out.

clue.text: Acetamide mixture might be too thin

indicators.note: a mixture combines things in a jumble, so the word's letters are stirred up

blocks.note: taken as written: the name of a chemical compound

explanation.surface: A chemistry note warns that a solution of this compound could turn out too dilute.
explanation.walkthrough: Acetamide is a real organic compound, which makes the chemistry surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated describes a body wasted away, abnormally thin through starvation or illness.

clue.text: Drunken bride succeeded causing wreckage

indicators.note: someone drunken reels about unsteadily, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A tipsy bride leaves a trail of destruction at the wedding party.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something broken or destroyed, just like wreckage.

clue.text: Deal with trendy copper's potential howlers

blocks.note: to deal is to trade
W is the abbreviation for with
something in is fashionable
d was the old British penny, a copper coin
the apostrophe-s supplies its letter

explanation.surface: A fashionable police officer is warned that some deals could lead to embarrassing blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: Howlers looks like blunders, but here it means things that howl, as strong winds do. Before 1971 a British penny was written d.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade winds blow steadily across the tropical oceans and, when strong, can howl.

clue.text: Compete in Lever business

blocks.note: to enter a race is to compete in it
to prise something is to lever it open

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to take on the giant Lever company in its own trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Lever invites thoughts of the Lever Brothers soap firm; it is simply a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a company or commercial undertaking, so it is a business.

clue.text: Down and dirty

blocks.note: first meaning: sad or low in spirits
second meaning: smutty or risqué, as in a crude joke

explanation.walkthrough: Down and dirty reads as one phrase meaning gritty; it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means depressed when feeling low, and indecent when describing a film or joke.

clue.text: Answer page expressing criticism in post

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
P is the abbreviation for page
pointed remarks carry deliberate criticism

explanation.surface: A letters page reply sharply criticises someone, sent by mail.
explanation.walkthrough: In post looks like it means in the mail; it means holding a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appointed has been formally given a job, so they are now holding that position.

clue.text: Catastrophe as in stride being disrupted

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other before any rearranging
something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner's catastrophe as they lose their stride mid-race.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden terrible event causing great damage, exactly what a catastrophe is.

clue.text: Works caught on — sure success one concludes

indicators.note: something that concludes comes at the very end of the sequence

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
a cert is a certainty, a sure winner
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A batsman caught out insists one more effort will surely succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cert, short for certainty, is British slang for a horse or bet bound to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerti are musical compositions for soloist and orchestra, and a composer's compositions are called works.

clue.text: Men, splitting apart, strangely maintaining correspondence

indicators.note: to split something is to break into it, so one piece goes into the middle of another
done strangely means done in an odd way, so the letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers who have separated oddly keep writing to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Correspondence suggests letters, but here it means matching in proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro rata is Latin for in proportion, keeping each share matched to its corresponding size.

clue.text: Flyer having arguments

blocks.note: to spar is to argue, trading verbal blows
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A pilot who is constantly getting into quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural arguments supplies two words for disputes, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small common bird, and in crosswords any bird can be called a flyer.

clue.text: Old impostor useless when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking means the word is judged by its pronunciation, not its spelling

blocks.note: idle means useless or ineffective, as in idle threats

explanation.surface: A washed-up con artist whose patter no longer fools anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a false god of ancient worship, an image pretending to divine power.

clue.text: Something excellent in cocaine user's epitaph?

blocks.note: rest in peace, the stock inscription on a gravestone
cocaine is taken by sniffing it up the nose

explanation.surface: A darkly comic gravestone joke about a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the joke: the gravestone would read rest in peace, snorter. Ripsnorter is informal British and Australian slang for a stunning example of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsnorter is a remarkable, outstanding thing, slang praise for anything first-rate.

clue.text: European in sauna developed sickness

indicators.note: a letter placed in a word goes inside it before rearranging
something developed has changed its form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A tourist in a Scandinavian steam room starts to feel ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the queasy feeling of wanting to vomit, a form of illness.

clue.text: Swimmer in location without current

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word surrounds the letter

blocks.note: a synonym
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A swimmer looks for a spot in the water away from the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like it means lacking; here it means on the outside of.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flat sea fish, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Diverted article leaving bottom exposed?

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: the indefinite article
your rear is your bottom
to out someone is to expose them publicly

explanation.surface: Somebody's trousers fall down, so the article's subject is left with backside on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic that is rerouted is sent along a different road, so it has been diverted.

clue.text: Get less following cut

indicators.note: less here means minus, so a letter is subtracted

blocks.note: to fetch is to go and get
f is the abbreviation for following, as in pp. 12f

explanation.surface: Someone gets a reduction after a spending cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design by cutting lines into metal or glass.

clue.text: See 9
Town regularly unlocked church for small sum

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: first and third letters of the word
a door unlocked can be opened
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: The town church was left unlocked, and a few coins were found in the collection box.
explanation.walkthrough: Twopence, pronounced tuppence, is two British pennies, a trifling amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Two pence is a tiny amount of money, so it stands for a trivially small sum.

clue.text: Dialect needing good English at all costs?

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
E is the abbreviation for English
from the phrase do or die, meaning whatever the cost

explanation.surface: A dialect that insists on proper English no matter what.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: or die is the tail of do or die, which means at any cost. Geordie is the speech of Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Geordie names both people from Tyneside and the distinctive regional dialect they speak.
